utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. First of all, our apologies for the delayed start. There were technical problems, some computer problems, but I hope that they are resolved. As yesterday, I would kindly ask the registrar to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Zdravko Tolimir. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And since these are the last sessions, I would kindly ask the Prosecution for the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. Peter McCloskey, together with Kweku Vanderpuye, Rupert Elderkin, Abeer Hasan, and Janet Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. My name is Zdravko Tolimir. Together with me is my legal advisor, Mr. Aleksandar Gajic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, very briefly I told you yesterday if there is anything which causes problems for you, health problems, you should indicate that to the Chamber immediately and you may request a pause, a break, so that you are able to conduct your closing arguments properly today. Because of the delayed start, we will consider if you need -- I should put it in a different way. We gave you one day, like the Prosecution yesterday, for your closing arguments. We lost 15 minutes. We will see how it develops today. And we still have the opportunity to have rebuttal and rejoinder arguments by tomorrow so that you shouldn't feel under pressure, time pressure, by giving your oral submissions. Mr. Tolimir, you have now the floor for your final oral submissions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to greet everybody present in this courtroom and may God give you all the blessings for all the good deeds that you are going to do. May God's will be done in these proceedings and not necessarily mine. Once again, thank you for the good communication with me. In the third amended indictment, the Prosecutor presented a lot of accusations against Tolimir and tried to corroborate those by speculative documents without any factual basis. At the very beginning, I have to say that the series of accusations that have been presented in the final brief were not present in the third amended indictment. However, since they're not founded, I do not need to defend myself by pointing to the facts that were not contained in the indictment. In the proceedings before this courtroom, in order to consider the facts as being established based on the indictment, they have to be proven beyond a reasonable doubt. And the Defence doesn't have to prove anything. It is the Prosecutor that has to prove -- the Prosecutor has to prove both the objective elements of all the charges that are contained in the indictment as well as the subjective elements of the crimes, the mens rea and the knowledge which is required for every crime. Criminal responsibility is always individual and all the facts have to be considered exclusively within the context of individual and subjective responsibility. In my final brief -- in his final brief the Prosecutor starts with the thesis: According to which Tolimir was one of the closest advisors and the person of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused be asked to slow down. It is impossible to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the Chamber wants to listen carefully to all your arguments. The interpreters asked you to slow down, otherwise they are not able to translate properly. Please read your text a little bit more slowly so that everybody can follow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. After the break I will try to provide the interpreters with a copy of what I'm reading and I apologise to them. The accused assumes criminal responsibility of General Mladic which was never proven and was not a matter of trial in these proceedings. The fact that during the war Tolimir was the assistant commander of the Main Staff of Republika Srpska for intelligence and security cannot serve to draw any conclusions about the criminal responsibility of Zdravko Tolimir. The idea of a court trial is to establish the truth and this is something what the Defence tried to do throughout the proceedings; however, that was not the case with the witnesses who struck a deal with the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please read slowly. Please read slowly. The interpreters can't follow. And if you have hard copies of your presentation, it could be delivered now to -- with the assistance of the court usher to the interpreters in the booths. That would be very helpful. Mr. Gajic --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have instructed my advisors to make those copies and they will do it with your leave, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the court usher that can be --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have one copy now. Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the meantime --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those witnesses have presented a series of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the meantime you should continue during the period when this matter is resolved, but please read slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This refers to the testimonies of those witnesses who presented a series of lies without any proof charging other persons, primarily Momir Nikolic and Witness PB-057 [as interpreted] who testified as viva voce witnesses, and then also Deronjic, whose contradictory testimony was adopted according to Rule 94 bis. In these proceedings we heard a number of members of UNPROFOR who were deployed in Bosnia and Herzegovina as peacekeepers. As a matter of fact, they actually contributed to the promulgation of the war and they acted in favour of BiH army. Let me remind you of the testimony that the Trial Chamber heard. For example, Witness Petar Skrbic, on transcript page 18649, testified that he attended a meeting which was also attended by Tolimir and commander of NATO for Europe Admiral Leighton Smith, who said that the role of NATO was to establish a balance of powers between the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Republika Srpska. If NATO representatives didn't hide that fact, today those who contributed the most to the implementation of that policy don't want to talk about that, and they are the representatives of the command structures of UNPROFOR. The way the role of UNPROFOR is presented today is best corroborated by the Dutch Institute for War Documentation which is partly in evidence in this case. I'm referring to P610, paragraph 2, in which it is stated: "Although it was stated differently in the public, the lawyers of the Royal Dutch Army prepared Dutch witnesses for testimonies and carefully examined their statements with the approval of Colonel Karremans. The progress of statements which may have opened some issues were deleted or reworked. At the end of day, the Ministry of Defence and the Prosecution did not pay attention to the Dutch Battalion but to Karadzic and to Mladic." False reporting happened during the war in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting. We want to have a clear and correct record. I think there is one mistake and we would like to clarify that. On page 5, line 8, there is a reference to the commander of NATO for Europe, Admiral Dayton Smith. I don't know if that is correct or if that is incorrect. Perhaps you repeat the name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. The name is Admiral Leighton Smith. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies and you should continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The false reporting that was happening during the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina was something that General Smith mentioned in one of statements at D192, and I quote: "Commanders sometimes submitted false reports to their superiors when they didn't want to hear things." One of the problems during the war in the territory of the former Yugoslavia was the question of the enclaves which had been proclaimed demilitarised and protected areas and nevertheless they were used as military strongholds. This was not only the case with Srebrenica and Zepa, but also with other enclaves, for example, Gorazde and Bihac which effectively served as a NATO army which became very prominent during the NATO aggression, the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia against the Republic of Serbia with the help of Rapid Reaction Forces. Without understanding the context within the developments happened during the period of the indictment, it would be impossible to see what the role of NATO and UNPROFOR was. I am referring to D324, page 2 in Serbian and 3 in English, and this is actually the statement by the officer of DutchBat van Duijn, who provided that statement before the commission of the Dutch parliament, and I quote: "There was no peace there; however, we were told to maintain that peace as best as we could. It was a political order to monitor how both sides maintained that peace." The Prosecutor charges Tolimir with participating and contributing to the implementation of two parts of joint criminal enterprise: Forcible removal and killing of males in Srebrenica. And based on that in the third amended indictment, it formulates three charges. None of the allegations which could serve as the basis for the conclusion of criminal responsibility are based on the facts which can be proven beyond reasonable doubt in these proceedings. The Prosecutor charges Tolimir with participation in the alleged criminal enterprise, whose alleged goal was to forcibly remove and deport Muslims from Srebrenica, and I quote: "The Prosecutor says that Tolimir largely contributed to the implementation of the joint criminal plan of the participants in the joint criminal enterprise." In that the moment when that alleged criminal plan was conceived, according to the Prosecution, was the 8th of March when the directive of number 7 was passed in 1995. The Prosecution also emphasises the important role of Tolimir in drafting of that directive; however, the Prosecution did not prove the concrete participation of Tolimir in the drafting of directive 7. Tolimir was not in charge of writing it nor was he involved in the wording of that directive. He played the role that in all the armies of the world is assigned to the assistant commanders for security and intelligence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness -- could the accused please be asked to slow down when reading. It is impossible to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the interpreters again asked you to slow down. They can't follow. And we want to have everything what you have to say to be reflected on the record. Please read slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise. And that role consists in submitting information about the enemy and proposing measures of intelligence and security support in keeping with the relevant regulations. As is stated in the final brief by the Prosecution in paragraph 164, I quote: "Mladic received proposals with regard to those elements of the directive that concerned that area -- their areas of work or their sectors. And if those elements were adopted, they would be included into the final version of the directive." In the parts of directive 7 which referred to the intelligence about the enemy and the intelligence and security support, there is nothing illegal. What is written in the parts of the directive in which there is information about the enemy and its intentions has been shown as completely truthful and was useful in practice during the war and after the war. Directive 7 in its challenge part which concerns the task of the Drina Corps was never changed. The directive 7 itself which was passed on the 8th of March, 1995, and which was passed by Commander Radovan Karadzic was soon replaced by directive 7/1 which was issued by the commander of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, General Ratko Mladic. In that directive there is no reference to the creation of unbearable conditions for the civilian population. The Prosecutor talks be all the actions that had to do with the enclaves and ties them with directive 7, including the alleged restrictions on the humanitarian aid convoys. However, in the relevant part of directive 7 it is stated, and I quote: "Daily planned combat activities to create conditions of total uncertainty." Delivering humanitarian aid is not a combat activity; therefore, it is not comprised by directive 7. Let me remind you, directive 7/1 which was passed soon after directive 7 is completely in keeping with the rules of international law of war and the role of Tolimir again consisted in submitting intelligence about the enemy. In paragraph 199 of its final brief, the Prosecution claims that the purpose of directive 7 was to deprive the population of Srebrenica and Zepa of the supplies that they needed for survival and thereby to cause a humanitarian catastrophe. However, there is no mention in any of the directives of this intention nor is there any evidence that the VRS deprived the population of the bare necessities. If the Prosecution speaks about the so-called ostensible restrictions, these kind of restrictions envisaged by directive 7 could not in any way be conducive to depriving the population of what they needed for survival. The evidence presented in this case demonstrate that the humanitarian convoys reached the enclaves even during the period when attacks on the Army of Republika Srpska were launched from these enclaves. There was one convoy scheduled for the 11th of July even which indicates that there was no planned activity for the capture of Srebrenica, but the plan was to separate Srebrenica and Zepa and to have these enclaves demilitarised. As one of the elements of the so-called JCE of the removal or deportation of the civilian population of Srebrenica and Zepa, alleges the purported restriction of humanitarian convoys. In paragraph 60 of the indictment, as well as in their final brief, they say and I read: "Tolimir imposed restrictions on UNPROFOR and humanitarian convoys." The allegations about so-called or purported illegal activities as presented in this case are not accurate and are not based on the established facts. Therefore, I assert that truth has to be established in every trial and that it cannot be based on what was being served as the propaganda apparatus of UNPROFOR and NATO. We have to make distinction between UNHCR convoys because their main purpose was to provide food for the population of Srebrenica; however, on more than one occasion they were abused and the commodities were delivered to the BH army in the enclaves. As for UNPROFOR, the purpose of these convoys was to deliver food and materiel for the needs of the UNPROFOR within the enclaves and they had nothing to do with the situation of the civilian population. As demonstrated by the evidence presented here, UNPROFOR was also involved in providing ABiH army and materiel. The totality of the evidence presented in this case, it can reasonably be concluded that both types of convoys were intended to create conditions for the Army of BH to be able to conduct offensive actions from the enclave in order to tie-up the territories of the enclave with the central territory of the Army of BH. First of all, concerning humanitarian aid or UNHCR convoys, neither Tolimir nor the Main Staff of the VRS did -- had no authorisation with regard to granting approval or denying approval for the movement of the convoys in the territory of Republika Srpska. In the relevant period of time, the responsibility for granting approvals for humanitarian aid was in the hands of a co-ordinating body for humanitarian operations that was headed by a civilian while the VRS exclusively had the task of providing security and checking of the convoys and to secure the routes of the movement of the convoys. The VRS didn't have an authority and didn't have any way of limiting the supply of humanitarian supply, nor did it impose any restrictions on humanitarian assistance. As for the responsibility for granting humanitarian convoys, an illustrative exhibit is D303, it is an order issued by the chief of the Main Staff of the VRS on the 31st of August, 1994, in which it explicitly says: "You know that the Main Staff of the VRS does not have any further authority or responsibility to grant the entry and the movement of the" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Tolimir please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I have to stop you because the interpreters have -- are now getting difficulties again. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I very much apologise for interrupting, but we have in the translation the chief of the Main Staff. Now there is a Chief of Staff of the Main Staff who we know is General Milovanovic and there is the commander of the Main Staff, as we know is Mladic. The chief of the Main Staff as translated is unclear who the General means, and I apologise to the General but our translators need to be able to fix that so we know whether you are talking about Milovanovic or Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It can easily be checked by looking into the document, D303, but this is a typical result of the speed of your submission. Again I have to ask you to read slowly. It's in your interest so that the Chamber is in the position to receive your full and the entire oral submission. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'm going to repeat what Mr. McCloskey has pointed out. Exhibit D303, an order issued by the chief of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska on 31st of August, 1994, explicitly says the following ... so we are talking about the chief. There was only one chief and that was Milovanovic. And I quoted this paragraph. In Exhibit D307, the document signed by General Mladic on the 16th of January, 1994, reads, and I quote: "Pursuant to the order issued by the president of Republika Srpska, Dr. Radovan Karadzic ..." Item 3 of the said order, confidential number 01-128/94, is amended in the following way: "All disputes with UNPROFOR and military observers shall be resolved exclusively through command of the corps of the Main Staff of the VRS. And as far as the international humanitarian organisations are concerned, this is going to be resolved through the government co-ordinating body for humanitarian aid." Concerning the responsibility for issuing decisions for humanitarian aid in the relevant period, that is to say from March of 1995, is clearly being indicated in Exhibit P689, which is a decision on setting up a state committee for co-operation with the United Nations international humanitarian organisations, which explicitly in Article 6 says: "The issuing of permits for humanitarian convoys and the movement of UN personnel and that of humanitarian organisations in the territory of Republika Srpska, shall be done pursuant to a decision taken by the committee and will be implemented by the co-ordinating body." Therefore, there is no evidence then in the course of 1994 and 1995 Tolimir was ever involved in the issues relating to humanitarian aid convoys for Srebrenica and Zepa. There is not a single document proving that that was the case and proving that Tolimir was at all involved in these matters or that he had any impact on the restrictions of humanitarian aid convoys. That was neither within the scope of his responsibility nor was it the responsibility of the VRS. The VRS's duty was to provide security for the convoys and to check them. In paragraph 211 of its final brief, the Prosecution says, and I quote: "Despite the fact that the state committee had been set up, it was the Main Staff of the VRS who had final authority to impose restrictions to humanitarian convoys at their own discretion." The Prosecution has no evidence to support this. On the contrary, the Main Staff staff of the VRS could not amend any decision taken by the co-ordinating body for the humanitarian aid as well as those taken by the committee. As said by Witness Slavko Kralj on transcript page 18383 when asked whether the Main Staff of the VRS was able to change the decisions approving the movement of convoys in the territory of Republika Srpska, he responded as follows: "This document could have been amended only based on the decision taken by the organ that had originally issued it." The Main Staff of the VRS did not have an authority to amend government documents. The duty of the Main Staff of the VRS was to issue a document, notifying the check-points about convoys that were given or denied permission to pass, which was a routine activity in which the chief of the staff or those who were entrusted with technical matters would deal with. This document in every aspect had to be in compliance with the decision of the co-ordinating body for humanitarian aid. In annex C of its final brief, the Prosecution makes reference to the restrictions of the humanitarian aid convoys by extracting pieces and parts of documents in which huge quantities of food and other necessities are stated as having reached the enclave. As an example of such restriction, the Prosecution says cylinders of oxygen, matches, plywood, oil, lubricants, et cetera, which is not necessary for the life of the civilian population; however, the Prosecution failed to analyse the quantities of food that reached Srebrenica and Zepa in the relevant period. From the documents that were presented to this Trial Chamber, it is clearly evident that considerable quantities of food and other bare necessities required for the life of civilians have, indeed, reached the enclaves. However, the problems with the commodities from the humanitarian aid are of a quite different nature because the humanitarian aid was primarily used in order to supply the Army of BH in the enclaves and the priority was given to its members. This was testified to by Witness PV-073 [as interpreted] on page 642 of the transcript, where he says that his son had been digging trenches for the BH army in exchange for food. All the humanitarian aid convoy problems are attributed by the Prosecution to the VRS; however, during the months preceding the attack on Srebrenica, the main problem was neither the VRS nor Republika Srpska, but rather the problems that existed between the Dutch Battalion and UNHCR. In the study of the Dutch Institute for War Documents, which is an Exhibit P619, page 6, reads that: "The Dutch Battalion also checked the convoys ..." And then it goes on to say: "On the 20th of June, another UNHCR convoy" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please slow down. It's impossible to follow. The interpreters are sometimes three or four lines behind you. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am quoting a portion of the study of the Dutch Institute. "On 20th June, another UNHCR convoy arrived in the enclave, this time with 56 tonnes of sugar, beans, salt, fish, flour, soaps, powder, milk, and biscuits. And once again the Dutch Battalion searched the convoy even more thoroughly than if it had been done by the VRS. According to the information provided by the UN military observers present on this location, the commander of the convoy objected to the inspection carried out by the Dutch Battalion and informed his staff thereof. The result was that this convoy was delayed until the next day until the Dutch Battalion changed its procedure." It goes on to say as follows on page 6 that: "The impact of these disagreements between the UNHCR on the one hand and the Dutch Battalion and Army of BH on the other was that the UNHCR convoys would be suspended for as long as the ABH army suspended or gave up on mandatory and thorough inspections. That would mean that the Dutch Battalion would have no reason to conduct any inspections of the convoy. Franken was not satisfied with this. He perceived it as an attempt to put the Dutch Battalion against the ABH and to make them as two confronting parties. His opinion was that the Dutch Battalion certainly did not want to act in accordance with what was dictated by the Army of BH, and in this case concerning UNHCR it is demonstrated that there was no willingness to allow the inspections of their convoys. They thought that adhering to their own principles and rules are much more important than the supply of the humanitarian aid, and they should not lay the blame on the Dutch Battalion and ABH for whatever happened."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the accused please continue from paragraph 28.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the interpreters asked you to continue from paragraph 28 again so that everything is on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In a nutshell, on the issue of these convoys, the failure to deliver humanitarian aid cannot be attributed to the alleged restrictions put in place by the VRS or any body or organ of Republika Srpska. Furthermore, Witness Slavko Kralj testified at page -- transcript page 18406 that in the month of May of 1995 convoys were not reaching the enclave during the VRS shelling campaign. They themselves suspended the movement of convoys without having even reported to anyone the fact that they had given up on some of these convoys. They were not restricted by either the co-ordinating body or the VRS. Simply put, these convoys did not reach check-points. According to the evidence of Witness Kralj, transcript page 18407, the same practice was in place during the NATO aggression on Republika Srpska in the months of September and October of 1995. Numerous pieces of evidence were adduced at trial which point to a continued practice of misuse of humanitarian aid convoys. Firstly, humanitarian aid was distributed among the members of the BH army and was used by the BH army in the enclaves, whereas humanitarian aid convoys were used as a means of smuggling in weapons and ammunition intended for the BH army. Since the enclaves were getting ready to engage in the operation of joining up the enclaves with the central part of the territory. By way of illustration, the convoy that was sent to Zepa in June of 1995, a large amount of ammunition was found hidden in flour sacks. We had occasion to see video-clip P2126 and Exhibit D78, wherein the Rogatica Brigade reported about having found a certain amount of ammunition in the convoy travelling to Zepa. We also saw Slavko Novakovic's reports speaking about the practice of misuse of these convoys, namely, Exhibits D73 and D214. Speaking about the practice of using UNHCR convoys as means of supplying BH army are documents such as Exhibits D197, D198, and D199. Let us mention here Exhibit D80 only. It bears the signature of Suljo Hasanovic, chief of the defence ministry branch in Srebrenica dated the 5th of June, 1995, wherein the defence secretariat in Tuzla was informed of the fact that a certain amount of food and fuel had been set aside for the needs of the BH army, and I quote: "After having been taken out of the humanitarian aid contingent which arrived in this area through the UNHCR and one of the batches of aid had been received from the Dutch Battalion." According to the rules of international humanitarian law, the goods intended for a civil population may not be placed at the disposal of military units. This was precisely done in Srebrenica and Zepa. The capabilities of the BH army to prepare and carry out sabotage and terrorist operations out of the enclaves and to work toward preparing the operation of joining up the enclaves with the central BH territory directly depended on the supplies coming from the humanitarian aid, and not only those but also on the supplies at the disposal of the DutchBat. Under those circumstances, Republika Srpska was entitled to restrict the use of humanitarian aid, but it had not done so. The allegation against Zdravko Tolimir, that he had participated in the imposition of restrictions on humanitarian aid convoys in order to create unbearable conditions, living conditions, for the civilian population, is unfounded in more than one way. The issue of convoys related to the logistic supplies for UNPROFOR is quite separate from the issue of UNHCR convoys which were intended for the humanitarian needs of the civilian population. Ever since its deployment there, UNPROFOR and the DutchBat in Srebrenica failed to perform their basic duties. The main duty of UNPROFOR was to demilitarise the enclave, but this had never even been attempted; quite the contrary. The UNPROFOR forces present in the enclave tolerated the fact that Muslims were armed, had regular meetings with them, and - as indicated by Exhibit P2120 - even developed a plan of joint action in the event the VRS would attack the enclave. And this plan was supposed to be kept secret even from UNMOs. Now, in paragraphs 228 and 229 of the Prosecution final brief, it is stated that because of the restrictions imposed on UNPROFOR by the VRS, UNPROFOR was unable to fulfil its mandate. However, the evidence clearly shows that UNPROFOR had not been engaged in fulfilling their mandate to begin with, namely, the demilitarisation of the enclaves, and instead proceeded to tolerate the BH army in the enclaves who had been arming busily and reorganising themselves in preparation for offensive combat. The fact that the VRS wasn't the party that was making the work of UNPROFOR impossible is clearly shown by the fact that ever since its deployment in the enclave UNPROFOR or the DutchBat did not enjoy freedom of movement. This is illustrated by the so-called Bandera Triangle, where 100 DutchBat members were captured immediately upon their deployment there. As stated by Witness Boering at transcript page 9032, we did not have actual freedom of movement. On the basis of evidence adduced at trial, one cannot conclude that the VRS restricted UNPROFOR in the fulfilment of their mandate; quite the contrary. The Republika Srpska army kept alerting UNPROFOR to the fact that they had been failing to fulfil their mandate and that they had been allowing the BH army to use the enclave as their military stronghold. At paragraph 228 of their final trial brief, the Prosecution mentioned the issue of air-lifts as a means of providing supplies for UNPROFOR. Exhibit P710, a telegram that General Janvier sent to Annan - and I repeat that, P710, the telegram sent by General Janvier to Annan on the 18th of April, 1995, indicates that this means of supplies would have had far-reaching consequences. The actual reasons motivating the air-lifts as means of supplies were presented by General Rupert Smith in their statement given to the Prosecution, D193, page 8. Therein he states: "I explained to Mladic that as an officer of the United Nations, I supported sanctions as a necessary part of the peace process. I also explained to him that the blockade of the enclave would have prevented me from carrying out the duty that I had in respect of my soldiers which could not be tolerated and which would result in the supplies being brought in by helicopter, and that would include NATO military operations as well." All of this was taking place in the period when Muslims were busy preparing themselves for the operation of joining up the enclaves with the central BH territory. Behind all these various requests there was the aspiration on the part of UNPROFOR to have convoys transit the Republika Srpska territory without any inspections or checks whatsoever. As indicated in the study produced by the Dutch Institute for War Documentation P619 [as interpreted], page 2, and I quote: "Smith wanted a decision to be taken at the highest possible level with a view to ensuring a freedom of movement rather than have that freedom depend on the circumstances prevailing or the various conditions, such as the possibility of checking convoys." Thereafter the VRS had to be notified of the fact that as part of the existing rules of engagement UNPROFOR was prepared to engage in combat to protect these convoys and to call in close air support. This is P169, page 2. However, the VRS consistently complied with the procedure proposed by UNPROFOR itself, specifically the issue of UNPROFOR convoys was regulated under two agreements, the general cessation of hostilities agreement, Exhibit P1011, and the agreement titled: "The Principles of the Freedom of Movement," which was stipulated at the proposal of UNPROFOR and signed by General Tolimir on behalf of the VRS and General Brinkman on behalf of UNPROFOR. This is Exhibit D77. The agreement regulated the way in which UNPROFOR convoys were to be cleared, were to move, and to be checked. This agreement, however, does not apply to humanitarian aid convoys and had nothing to do with the supply of humanitarian aid of the civilian population. The witness who was best placed to speak to the issue of the way in which decisions were taken with regard to UNPROFOR convoys and to the role of Tolimir therein was Slavko Kralj. And the Trial Chamber should pay due attention to his evidence. General Tolimir and General Gvero were representatives of the VRS in the central joint commission at the meetings of which UNPROFOR convoy movements were negotiated as well as other issues relating to the freedom of movement. Tolimir did not have the authority to either approve or deny the approval for the movement of convoys. He could merely provide his opinion on the information arising from the meetings of the joint central commission. The decisions were taken either by commanders or chiefs of staffs. Or, in their absence, the officer who was entrusted with that task by his commander. Tolimir and Gvero participated in the procedure where certain requests by UNPROFOR were examined - there was evidence adduced to that effect as well - because they were members of the joint central commission. This was confirmed by Witness Kralj at transcript page 18281: "At the meetings of the joint central commission, the type of goods and the quantities of goods that may be transported were discussed." Secondly, it was proven at trial that in deciding on approvals for UNPROFOR convoys, care was taken of the quantities that are required for UNPROFOR purposes in order to allow it to operate and to have sufficient foodstuffs for soldiers. The goods that could have been used as supplies for the BH army and that were not necessitated by the DutchBat were not given clearance, as was the case, for instance, with large quantities of Plexiglass, ski gear, and similar. On the issue of weapons and ammunition, the DutchBat in Srebrenica and the Ukrainian Battalion in Zepa were hostages of the BH army which was able to disarm them at will and to seize their weapons. By way of illustration, the instance where weapons and ammunition were seized off the Ukrainian Battalion in Zepa, Exhibit D55, paragraph 94. Now, there is also Exhibit D105 which clearly speaks about the fact that the weapons and equipment intended for UNPROFOR could possibly also have been used for the purposes of the BH army. This is one of the reports produced by Avdo Palic and intended for the BH army General Staff dated 16 July 1995 which reads, and I quote: "We have been disarming UNPROFOR as per the previously received instructions." In other words, there was a plan to disarm UNPROFOR, and that plan was held by the Muslims in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Prosecutor's thesis that the situation involving UNPROFOR convoys contributed to the disabling of the UNPROFOR and that that's why they couldn't demilitarise the area is at least unfounded, if not more than that, and it shows the speculativeness of the Prosecutor's argument. Namely, UNPROFOR in the enclaves had enough weapons and ammunition from the moment that they arrived in the enclave. From the moment they arrived in the enclave, they did not take any serious measures in order to disarm the BiH army in the demilitarised zones. The UNPROFOR whose duty was to demilitarise the enclave never used weapons against the BiH army. Whatever weapons they had, they placed against the VRS on the 9th and 10th and 11th of July, 1995, and in addition to that the convoys were tendentiously used against the VRS. The true situation with the convoys is demonstrated by D304 which is a document issued by Mr. Akashi on the 1st of March, 1995. That document shows the way the BiH army treated UNPROFOR. In a nutshell in paragraph 5 on page 4 it is stated, and I quote: "First of all, the Bosnian government and Bosnia and Herzegovina are abusing the relative peace which was established after the agreement on the cessation of hostilities was signed in order to put financial pressure on UNPROFOR with regard to the agreements." I continue with the quote: "Secondly, taking into account the reorganisation of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the gathering of a large quantity of forces and logistics support in the key areas, we believe that an attack is in the offing and that that attack could be launched as soon as the weather conditions improve. "Thirdly, the intention of the government, inter alia, is to convince the international community that the agreement on the cessation of hostilities is not functioning, and in that way they want to discredit the Bosnian Serbs. As a matter of fact, the Bosnian government is the one which has caused more problems because of the introduction of new restrictions on the freedom of movement and that's why they refuse to attend the meetings of the Joint Commission. That is why UNPROFOR has reached a stalemate and the problems cannot be resolved in an adequate way through the work of the Joint Commission. On the other hand, the restrictions that the Serbs have introduced have been largely weakened, although they are still in charge and they still control the delivery of fuel into the enclaves." The Prosecutor speaks about the alleged participation of Tolimir in the restriction of UNPROFOR convoy in paragraph 60(A) and portrays that involvement as an attempt to create unbearable conditions for the civilian population of Srebrenica and Zepa. This allegation is completely unfounded, since UNPROFOR convoys did not have anything to do with the position of the civilian population in the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa. The Prosecutor points out that the goal of the VRS was to create unbearable conditions for the population of the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa. However, among the multitude of evidence which prove that this was not the goal of the VRS is also a statement by Major Franken that he provided to the Prosecutor. This is P607, which says, inter alia: "During that period the Serbs proposed to the Muslims to trade with them at the prices that prevailed in the black market in the enclaves. After several rounds of negotiations, the civilian authorities of the enclaves allowed the Serbs to supply the enclaves. We insisted that goods should be sold at the market price or what would have been the market price and that the Dutch Battalion should not have any commercial role in that." This fitted well within our own idea of normalising a relationship with -- among the warring parties. Very soon rumours spread that that initiative did not bode well with the groups that controlled the black market. The local military authorities stated that the ban came from the top echelons of the military leadership although similar things functioned well in Gorazde. I suppose that the initiative to boycott the trade actually came from the military leadership in the enclave." The proposal that was made by the Serbs with regard to establishing trade relationship with Srebrenica is completely contrary to the Prosecutor's thesis and the allegations that there was an intention to create a totally unbearable conditions for the population of the enclave. One of the contributions in the alleged joint criminal enterprise regarding the expulsion from the civilian population from the enclaves is the operation which was carried out by the 10th Sabotage Detachment on the 23rd June, 1995. In paragraph 890 of the Prosecutor's final brief, the Prosecutor proposes a totally uncorroborated allegation according to which, and I quote: "Tolimir approved the engagement of the 10th Sabotage Detachment in the implementation of terrorist activities against the civilian population of Srebrenica with a view to making the living conditions in the enclaves unbearable."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please be asked to slow down when reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I have to stop you again. The interpreters asked that you slow down while reading. You are all the time reading your own text and the quotations. Please bear in mind that many people have to follow. Slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise to the interpreters. First of all, besides the fact that the facts are unfounded, the Prosecutor did not include that in the indictment. In that operation, or rather, Colonel Salapura testified about the operation by the 10th Sabotage Detachment. He was engaged in the preparations for that operation and he testified that: "It was a diversionary operation that did not have any consequences," and that "implementing that diversionary action was just an admonishment to the forces in Srebrenica not to take action against the VRS." First of all, there is no proof that Tolimir approved that operation. Indeed, there could be no evidence to that effect because Tolimir was not in a position to either order the use or use the 10th Sabotage Detachment. That detachment was an independent unit of the Main Staff of the VRS which was directly subordinated to the commander, i.e., to the Chief of Staff. That military operation had not been directed against the civilian population which is clearly demonstrated by P2200 issued on the 21st of June, 1995. That document was signed by Colonel Salapura. And this document speaks about the use of the 10th Sabotage Detachment. The 10th Sabotage Detachment was provided clear instructions in paragraph 1, and I quote from that paragraph: "To collect data, to plan and to implement the task. The person responsible for all that is the commander of the 10th Sabotage Detachment and the chief of the intelligence department of the Drina Corps." In paragraph 6 of the document it says: "When implementing the task, strictly adhere to the following: "UNPROFOR members should not be threatened, avoid inflicting casualties among the women and children." This document shows that the Prosecutor's allegation about that operation is completely unfounded and that its objective was not to attack the civilian population or to intimidate it. That diversionary action was not an attack against the civilian population which is also corroborated by a report by Ramiz Becirovic who drafted it on the 27th of June, 1995, and which says that nobody was hurt during that operation. If anybody had been hurt, Ramiz Becirovic's report would certainly have contained that information. In any case, nothing is said about Tolimir's actions in the third amended indictment as Tolimir's contribution to the alleged joint criminal enterprise, and that's why this operation by the 10th Sabotage Detachment is not relevant when it comes to considering criminal -- Zdravko Tolimir's criminal responsibility. The Prosecutor regards the attack against Srebrenica unlawful. For example, in paragraph 259 of the final brief, the Prosecutor says: "The attack against the Srebrenica enclave had two legitimate military goals: To achieve the demilitarisation of the enclave and thus disabling the 28th Division from launching attacks from the enclave and to completely cut the contact between the two enclaves. However, creating unbearable conditions for the population of the enclaves constituted the violation of the international laws." Moreover, by interpreting General Smith's testimony the Prosecutor states, and I quote that: "The attack against the enclave was not the only choice for the VRS." The Prosecutor erroneously states that the goal of the Krivaja 95 operation was to create unbearable conditions for the population of Srebrenica, whereas he never mentions the real reason for attacking Srebrenica -- or rather, he mentions the real attack against Srebrenica. The attack that was launched on the 6th of July, 1995, was the only possible situation primarily because of the fact that the BiH army had carried out operations to link-up the territory of the enclaves with the central part of the territory during the period of time when the all-out aggression against the territory of Republika Srpska was being prepared. If the VRS had not carried out an attack against Srebrenica and Zepa, in the following months it would have faced offensive operations at several fronts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, it's now over 15 minutes before 4.00. It's time for the first break although we started a little bit later, and I think it would be a convenient time for our first break. For your benefit and for the benefit of the interpreters, I would kindly ask you to make sure, together with Mr. Gajic, that all interpreters have the text of your submissions and also the court reporter should be provided with one copy. We adjourn and resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir and Mr. Gajic, can you tell us if the interpreters and the court reporter have now a hard copy each? I see you nodding, Mr. Gajic. Thank you very much. But nevertheless, I would kindly remind you again to slow down while reading. It's not possible to follow in that speed. And again, it's in your interest. If we lose sentences which are important, then it's not in your interest and therefore you should really read slowly. Please continue, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have left out one sentence from the previous paragraph which says: "The exclusive reasons for Krivaja 95 are legal and legitimate." Republika Srpska had a right to attack the ABH in Srebrenica and Zepa and claims pursuant to Article 60 of Protocol I to the Geneva Conventions; namely, due to frequent, serious, and fundamental violations of the agreement on demilitarisation which included extensive attacks from the enclaves, the VRS was relieved of its obligation to treat this area as a demilitarised zone and had the right to attack it. The reasons for the attack on Srebrenica and the aims of the attack are clearly stated in Exhibit P1202, which is an order for active combat operations issued at the -- by the then-commander of the Drina Corps, General Zivanovic, which contains as the reason for active combat operations as such: "We estimate that in the forthcoming period the enemy is going to intensify its operations towards the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps and to intensify offensive operations focusing on the Tuzla, Zvornik, and Kladanj-Vlasenica axis with the parallel and simultaneous engagement of the 28th Infantry Division from the enclave of Srebrenica and Zepa in order to cut off the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps and to link up the enclaves with the central territory of the former BiH under the control of the Muslim forces. In recent days, particularly active are Muslim forces from Zepa and Srebrenica enclave. Sabotage and terrorist groups are being infiltrated who are attacking and torching villages, killing civilian population, and smaller units are being sent to the areas around Zepa and Srebrenica enclave, particularly persistent in trying to link up the enclaves and creating this corridor ..." and then it goes on to say about the plans of the Muslims. There is an abundance of evidence which show that the linking up of the enclave with the central territory of the BH Federation was the main and the sole reason for the operation Krivaja 95. I make reference to P2369, a document produced on the 9th of November, 1994, by Brigadier General Enver Hadzihasanovic from the Supreme Command of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, addressed to the commander of the 8th OG Srebrenica, Naser Oric, which details the plan for the implementation of this idea which is defined in the following way: "By means of active combat operations, liberate the temporarily occupied territories of Bosnia-Herzegovina, namely, Bratunac, Vlasenica, Sekovici, Zvornik, and Kalesija municipalities, and link up free territories of Zepa and Srebrenica with the free territories of Zvornik, Kalesija and Zivinice, with a view of creating a permanent free corridor for delivering supplies to the population and logistical support of units of the BH army and creating a basis for further liberation of north-Eastern Bosnia as a whole." This plan was something that both the VRS and UNPROFOR knew about because it is explained in that way in the final brief of the Defence in paragraphs 414 to 419. The fact that the aim was to militarily defeat ABH in order to prevent the linking up of the enclaves with the central territory of BH is described by General Mladic in a conversation that he had with General Smith. Namely in the statement that General Smith gave to the Prosecution, and that is D193, page 9, General Smith speaks about the meeting that he had with General Mladic, at which General Mladic explained to him, I quote: "That he was expecting an attack, a Bosnian attack, from eastern enclaves in which case he would attack the enclaves in order to destroy the ABH but would be respecting in doing so his interpretation of the borders of the safe zone and not the interpretation of the UN." And then Smith concludes as follows: "Finally, after this series of meetings I reached the conclusion that the Bosnian Serbs have become aware that further fighting is unavoidable and that some sort of solution must be found during the year. The eastern enclaves were too strong and the BH army deployed within these enclaves constituted a clear threat, particularly because the army of the Bosnian Serbs felt that there was a possibility for them to be faced by attacks on several fronts." Everything that was happening in and around the enclaves was the consequence exclusively of total unpreparedness on the part of UNPROFOR to implement the agreement on demilitarisation reached in 1993 and the agreement on general cessation of hostilities admitted into evidence as P1011 in whose Article 6: "The parties undertake to adhere to the agreement on demilitarisation of Srebrenica, Zepa without delay and in full the one that was concluded on the 24th of May, 1993. Unfortunately, instead of general cessation of hostilities and demilitarisation of the enclave, the ABH in Srebrenica and in Zepa were arming themselves and reorganising themselves in order to carry out the operation of linking up the enclaves with the central part of BH. In addition to representatives of the VRS, the ABH and the Croats, the agreement was signed as witnesses thereby guaranteeing its implementation, representatives of UNPROFOR, namely, General Michael" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please stop and wait. The interpreters haven't finished the sentences you were reading before. You should from time to time look at the transcript and to see if it is still going on, and then you shouldn't start the next sentence. Please be very careful. The last words were -- which are recorded were: "Representatives of UNPROFOR, namely, General Michael" and then it stopped. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Michael Rose and Yasushi Akashi. This agreement was binding for UNPROFOR, including General Smith, General Nicolai, and the DutchBat. Instead of honouring the agreement on the general cessation of hostilities, Republika Srpska was under severe sanctions whilst the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, contrary to the arms embargo was arming itself and reorganising itself and carrying out offensive operations within the framework of the so-called spring offensive. Intensive sabotage and terrorist operations launched from the enclave are documented, inter alia, by following exhibits: D1, D16, D52, D53, D62, and D76. In Exhibit D238, which is an intelligence report dated 26th June 1995, on page 2 it is said: "The Muslim forces, the 28th Division, on the night between the 25th and 26th June of this year, launched an offensive from the Srebrenica and Zepa enclave by infiltrating our territory with several sabotage and terrorist groups. They blocked UNPROFOR in Srebrenica under the pretext that they failed to protect the demilitarised zone. One should not rule on the possibility that some members of the UNPROFOR were disarmed. The aim of this operation was most probably to link up our forces and to create favourable conditions for the operations by the 24th and the 26th Division from the direction of Kalesija, Zivinice, and Kladanj. Even the Prosecution witness Momir Nikolic stated in this courtroom, and it's recorded on transcript pages 12565 and 12566, and confirmed his statement given to the Dutch Institute for War Documentation, the number of the statement is D206 which reads, I quote: "The exodus from the enclave took the VRS by surprise. They had thought that Oric had gone to Tuzla and attempted to try and set up a corridor towards Srebrenica. Thereby, they would try to make a breakthrough to both territories. According to this scenario, the 2nd Corps would set off from Crni Vrh. From a corridor thus created, the Muslims would then cleanse the remaining territory towards the Drina and cleanse it of all Serbs. According to the information that the VRS had, it -- this plan should have been implemented between the 20 and the 25th of July, 1995. That is the reason why Oric and other officers left the enclave. The Muslim side did not make any particular effort to keep the plan about the corridor secret. Moreover, they even make -- made an announcement to this effect in order to create fear among the Serbian population. Twenty thousand Muslim forces were tasked with the cleansing of the other valley. While he was sitting at the same table with UNPROFOR, Oric reportedly claimed that he was the only one capable of organising between 10- and 15.000 soldiers in the 28th Division. That was sufficient to take the reports about the forming of the corridor seriously. Even the inhabitants of the enclave were perhaps informed about the planned breakthrough. In the recent months, large quantities of ammunition reached the enclave as well as doctors and medicines. In May and June 1995, the traffic between Zepa and Srebrenica considerably intensified. By following these kind of developments, the VRS asked for a meeting with the Muslims in Karremans office. However, Karremans failed to invite the Muslims. This was paragraph 41. These as well as other pieces of evidence clearly show why the Operation Krivaja was carried out, although the Prosecution does not cite any specific allegations and charges. In paragraph 889 of their final brief, they state that Tolimir contributed to the JCE by providing regular intelligence report about Srebrenica and Zepa in order to support the forthcoming attacks. First of all, providing intelligence information to the commander and other units and institutions was not something that was specifically conducted in the period between March and July 1995. Instead, Tolimir was doing that same thing throughout the whole war and there are several hundred such reports admitted into evidence. By providing these reports, Tolimir carried out his duty of the assistant commander for intelligence and security. As time has shown, his reports were accurate and if by doing so and by knowing that the Muslims were preparing attacks in order to link up the territories of the enclave with the centre part of the territory held by ABH, Tolimir did not contribute to any kind of joint criminal enterprise. This is merely the collection of information and intelligence about the enemy, i.e., the BH army who throughout the whole period of the war was enjoying the protection of UNPROFOR and NATO and which were used for joint operations of the ABH, the Croatian armed forces, and NATO Rapid Reaction Forces and a joint aggression against the Republika Srpska towards the end of the war. The attack on Srebrenica was not an attack on the civilian population, nor did it have anything to do with causing harm to the civilian population. We had occasion to see a video, which is the Srebrenica video, indicating that on the 11th of July there was still population housing their apartments in the centre of Srebrenica and that there was provocation fire coming out directed at the VRS. And the fact that the target of this attack was not the civilian population was also demonstrated by what Witness Kingori stated, namely, that there was surprisingly few victims. He said as much on transcript page 5571. The Srebrenica proper was riddled with military targets, since private homes, housing developments, public buildings, the PTT building, as well as other buildings were used for the purposes of armed formations, that's to say the BH army. This is corroborated by the Prosecution Exhibit P957 which is a document dated 22nd February 1995, which contains information about the buildings used by the BH army. Let me repeat the exhibit number, it's P957. Excellent. Thank you. A number of documents speak to the fact that neither operation Krivaja 95 nor the attack on Srebrenica were directed against the civilian population. Among these documents are the ones authored by Zdravko Tolimir. The way Tolimir went about the issue of the protection of UNPROFOR and the civilian population can be clearly found in several documents. Firstly, in Exhibit D85, a letter Tolimir sent to General Krstic on the 9th of July, 1995, which reads, among others: "Special attention is to be given to the protection of UNPROFOR members and the civilian population." Exhibit D41 is another document that clearly indicates the approach taken toward the civilian population of Srebrenica. In the memo dated 9th July 1995 sent by Tolimir to the Generals Gvero and Krstic, it is stated, and I quote: "Pursuant to the order of the president of Republika Srpska, issue an order to all combat formations participating in combat around Srebrenica to secure the highest possible protection and security for all members of UNPROFOR and civilian Muslim population. Give a clear order to your subordinates that they are to refrain from destroying civilian targets unless forced to do so by the strong resistance from the enemy. Prohibit -- issue a prohibition of the torching of housing buildings and make sure that the civilian population and prisoners of war are treated in compliance with the Geneva Conventions of 12th August 1949." In other words, the evidence that has been presented here shows that Tolimir cannot be attributed the intent necessary for an attack on the civilian population. Tolimir did not order or issue any orders in the course of combat, nor was he present in Srebrenica. A commander of an operation will involve all the forces, assets, and the rest in the operation under his command, and in the course of that operation, in order to ensure that there is unity of command and singleness of command, all those involved in the operation are subordinated to the commander concerned. The position of the UNPROFOR was a threat to the VRS from the very start and they threatened with air-strikes against VRS positions around the enclave.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter asks the accused to start again from that sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the interpreters ask to start again with the sentence because they didn't get everything.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The blocking positions and the green order were, according to the evidence adduced in this case and as indicated by the Prosecution in paragraph 289 of the trial brief, erected on the evening of the 9th of July, 1995. However, the VRS Main Staff did not issue a single order to open fire on UNPROFOR; quite the contrary. The VRS Main Staff issued orders not to open fire on UNPROFOR and the civilian population. This is indicated, among others, by Exhibit D69, a memo which was designated as urgent and sent by Milenko Zivanovic from the Pribicevac forward command post personally to General Krstic and the VRS Main Staff personally to Zdravko Tolimir, and it was a memo intended for their information which reads, and I quote: "The Main Staff has ordered that you do not open fire on UNPROFOR and that you avert any possible surprise attacks and intentions on the part of the Muslims to tie or to link up Srebrenica and Zepa. I wish you plenty of luck and extend greetings. General Tolimir." Evidence was adduced in this case about the so-called blocking positions erected by the DutchBat on the 9th July 1995. At paragraph 292 of their final trial brief, the Prosecution stated, and I quote: "The idea advanced by the Defence that the blocking positions were conceived with the objective of provoking the VRS into opening fire against members of the peace forces makes no sentence, in view of the fact that the members of the peace forces and the civilian population had been under fire for days and that nothing needed to be done to provoke the VRS into opening fire." As demonstrated by Exhibit D69, the VRS Main Staff ordered that no fire should be opened on UNPROFOR, whereas the view that blocking positions were conceived with the objective of provoking the VRS into opening fire on UNPROFOR positions in order to ensure fire support was not, in fact, an idea advanced by the Defence. It is a fact based on the evidence adduced in this case. The allegations advanced by the Prosecution are contrary to what the Prosecution witness stated, namely, General Nicolai, and what van Duijn said before the commission of the Dutch parliament. General Nicolai in a statement given to the Prosecution, which is D70, stated the following at page 10, and I quote: "On Sunday, the 9th, the VRS resumed their attack and it became quite clear that they were not only attacking the southern part of the enclave but that their attack had the objective of the town of Srebrenica. This led to several exchanges of consultations between the staff in Sarajevo and the staff in Zagreb, and the main issue discussed in these exchanges was under which conditions would the use of fire-power -- of air fire be allowed. Zagreb clearly stated that General Janvier was not willing to resort to this ultimate measure before the DutchBat used their own weapons. He wanted certain other steps to be taken before air-strikes would be resorted to. As a result of these consultations, we issued -- we gave an order to the DutchBat to take up blocking positions south of the town of Srebrenica so that should the VRS attack the town it would not only constitute an attack on the civilian population but also an attack on UNPROFOR units. Thereby, all the necessary conditions for the use of air-strikes would be met. The Dutch Battalion complied with this order." Consequently, the reason why blocking positions were erected was without any doubt to create conditions to ensure that the VRS positions can be bombed. That a green order had been issued is shown by a number of exhibits in this case. Witness Franken stated at transcript page 3453 in lines 23 to 25, and I quote: "By having issued a green order, we were engaging with the VRS and the VRS became a target. And in fact quite -- what was realistic and correct was quite the contrary." And at page 3484 he explained that: "The fact that the green order was issued changed the mandate of the Dutch Battalion and that the restrictions that had been there on the use of armed force disappeared in fact." Exhibit D324 is the statement given by van Duijn to the Dutch parliamentary commission investigating Srebrenica and at page 4 he speaks about this green order and the nature of the order, and I quote: "The order was issued as green, which means that there was a higher tendency toward hostilities. We had been preparing for that order by trying to collect as much equipment as we had at our disposal and by deploying our soldiers. We next went and took up positions. The order was that we should return fire if fired upon and that we should first fire above their heads, and I mean of the Serbs, and later right at them. This was part of the combat order by Captain Groen. "In fact, it was a green order which made use of certain blue assets and this isn't the proper way of going about it. If you are complying with a green order, you have to resort to camouflage and make sure that you carry out your operation with an element of surprise. You can surely not go about it by taking up positions out in the open, without any cover, and with white vehicles and blue helmets." On that same page there is something to be learned from the question put by a member of the parliamentary commission. He made a statement to van Duijn and put a question to him. "A month earlier the Dutch Battalion was engaged in drills in these blocking positions. Did you participate in these drills yourself?" Van Duijn's answer was that he had not taken part in these drills. In other words, the DutchBat was ready to take up blocking positions at a time when the attack on the enclave had not even been in the planning stage. Had the purpose of these blocking positions been -- or rather, that the purpose of these blocking positions was to attract VRS fire is also proved by the following quotation at page 5. Mr. Baker's question: "You took up these positions in a favourable moment. You've already told us that it was supposed to be carried out with fire support. Was the purpose of these blocking positions also to attract the fire of the Bosnian Serbs as a way of bringing about fire support? Van Duijn's answer to that was, I quote: "I realised at a later stage that this was what it was all about." In response to yet another question on page 6 van Duijn answered: "At first we indeed fired above their heads. I don't recall exactly what was our order. That was just one of the orders of the many issued by Captain Groen, but I know that I issued my artilleryman an order to shoot at the Serbian soldiers as soon as he saw them." Actions by the DutchBat on the ground were such that on the one hand, together with the BiH army, they participated in combat activities against the Serbs, and they did everything that they could in order to shell the VRS positions. On the other hand, they sought protection from the VRS. In this case no evidence was adduced to the fact that members of the Dutch Battalion who feared Muslims and joined the VRS side and that in doing that they were exposed to any irregular treatment. In order to prove Tolimir's role in Operation Krivaja, the Prosecutor alleges that Tolimir participated in the co-ordination and control of Krivaja 95 attack and providing support to that attack. That's in paragraph 891. The allegation provided by the Prosecutor can be found within the context of the charges contained in paragraph 60 of the third amended indictment, wherein it is stated that Tolimir contributed to the joint criminal enterprise by disabling UNPROFOR's military capabilities, including the prevention and control of the international protection for the enclaves from the outside, including air-strikes and international monitors." And it says: "By his contact with UNPROFOR, he helped to disable UN capabilities during the attack against Srebrenica. To be more specific, he lied to the UNPROFOR and co-ordinated with other officers from the Main Staff and in the subordinated units." This Prosecutor's allegation is unfounded from several aspects and one of them is the fact that it is legally unfounded. Since those contacts were those that Tolimir maintained as part of his regular duties. First of all, the Prosecution claims in paragraph 270 of its final brief that Tolimir was in the Main Staff of the VRS and in the command of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica. The Prosecution's allegation that on the 9th of July Tolimir was in Vlasenica is not corroborated by any evidence. The Prosecutor evokes D85 in which it conveys the contents of a conversation with General Nicolai. First of all, Nicolai called the Main Staff and not the command of the Drina Corps. The command of UNPROFOR did not have a link with the Drina Corps in Vlasenica. Evidence D85 is a document issued by the command of the Drina Corps on the 9th of July, 1995, which was sent to the command of the Drina Corps at the forward command post at Pribicevac to the attention of General Krstic as well as to the sector for intelligence and security of the Main Staff to the attention of General Tolimir for his information. It turns out that Tolimir sent a document to himself in order to inform himself about its contents. It really doesn't make any sense. The only reasonable conclusion that one can draw from an analysis of this document is that Tolimir sent a similar document or a document with the same contents from the General Staff and somebody in the Drina Corps, probably General Zivanovic, forwarded it by having first changed the heading. Since this telegram was sent as urgent, it seems that the sender did not have the time or indeed the need to add to it who the telegram was sent by or anything else for that matter. It is important to mention that in this document it is particularly stated, and I quote: "Pay special attention to the protection of UNPROFOR members and the civilian population." In other words, Tolimir was in the Main Staff of the VRS. He conveyed his communication with the UNPROFOR and he insisted on his men protecting UNPROFOR members and the civilian population, despite the fact that they threatened him with air-strikes that had already been planned. This is also demonstrated by evidence D137. That document shows that that zone had to be created around Srebrenica and that's a quote and that death zone had to be created by NATO aircraft. Tolimir did not lie to the UNPROFOR when he alerted them to the fact that the Muslims were using UNPROFOR APCs. Let's remind ourselves of Franken's testimony on page 3456 of the transcript. To the question as to whether he knew anything about the fact that checks were made, after the General Staff of the VRS had warned them that the Muslims were using six combat vehicles that were painted white, he answered, and I quote what Franken said: "I know that sometime in April I received a report from one of my observation posts. They reported to me that two APCs 60, eight-wheelers, painted in white arrived from south and that they drove into the enclave at a very high speed. We tried to stop them. However -- or rather, to confirm that they were there. However, after that we never saw them again. During the attack we did not see them being used." On page 3459, lines 16 through 19, Franken testified that in the logistics report he saw that members of the Ukrainian Battalion in Zepa reported a loss of six APCs. Exhibit P1225 proves that those APCs were indeed used. That is an order for the attack against Zepa issued on the 13 July 1995. In paragraph 7 of this document, page 3, it is stated, and I quote: "Be prepared for action against APCs which the Muslim army had stolen from UNPROFOR and it is now using them against our own forces." The Prosecutor alleges in paragraph 893 of the final brief that during the operation Tolimir lied to UNPROFOR in order to try to buy time, that he manipulated them in order to make it easier to the VRS to occupy the enclave and to forcibly remove the population." The Prosecutor alleges that Tolimir's actions neutralised in the key, final phase of the Srebrenica operation the UNPROFOR troops so that UNPROFOR did not succeed in blocking the VRS attack and thus saving the enclave." General Nicolai and General Janvier, with whom Tolimir communicated within the telephone, did not make their decisions based on what Tolimir had told them. Rather, they made their decisions based on their own intelligence, the intelligence that they received from the Dutch Battalion and in keeping with what they had intended to achieve. During that period of time, Tolimir performed his regular duties and he responded to UNPROFOR requests in the course of the operation during which UNPROFOR from the day one sided up with the BiH army, which had been previously planned at a meeting between Karremans and representatives of the BiH army. With them he co-ordinated his own activities and he used all of the available force against the VRS on the 9th, 10th, and 11th July, and that also included air-strikes on the 11th July 1995. The objective of the attack against the enclave, as we have already demonstrated, was not to attack the civilian population or the UNPROFOR which is clear from several documents that Tolimir sent during the relevant period. The attack against the enclave was aimed at its demilitarisation, at attacking and fighting against armed terrorist groups, and those were legitimate objectives and those were legitimate targets. The Prosecution does not have a single piece of evidence based on which it could prove that Tolimir's participation in that operation was against the civilian population. The contrary is true. He regularly issued instructions not to attack the civilian population and not to attack UNPROFOR. Tolimir's participation in the attack against Srebrenica cannot be qualified as an attack against the civilian population. His actions and negotiations with UNPROFOR during which he reported to the UNPROFOR on what he had received from the ground, he's taking measures in order to remove the bodies are not actions that would incriminate him. In paragraph 60(B) of the indictment, the Prosecution charges Tolimir with the participation in the military arming of the Muslim forces --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, again you are asked by the interpreters to slow down. You should repeat the last sentence beginning with the words: "In paragraph 60(B) of the indictment ..."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In paragraph 60(B) of the indictment, the Prosecution charges Tolimir with the participation in the military defeat of the Muslim forces. Allegedly, he did that by, and I quote: "He contacted the forward command post of the Drina Corps and the president of Republika Srpska, Radovan Karadzic, with regard to the combat operations surrounding Srebrenica and the decision on taking Srebrenica." This charge is unfounded, i.e., it cannot be considered any sort of contribution to the alleged forcible removal of the population of Srebrenica. Namely, Exhibit D41, which is Tolimir's document issued on the 9th of July, 1995, is clear with regard to the fact that the target of the attack was neither the civilian Muslim population nor the UNPROFOR. In this document it is stated, and I quote: "I order you not to set residential buildings on fire and I order you to treat the civilian population in agreement with the Geneva Conventions dated the 12th of August, 1949." The text of this instruction is clear. The Prosecutor considers the evacuation of the Srebrenica population unlawful, i.e., the Prosecutor claims that that was the case of a forcible removal of the population. The decision on the evacuation of the civilian population is not Tolimir's decision. It was not a decision by the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska or the civilian bodies of Republika Srpska. That decision was taken at the level of the United Nations and by the authorities in Srebrenica. What was the position of Republika Srpska towards the civilian population of Srebrenica? This can be seen from Exhibit D41 which is Tolimir's document which says that the civilian population had to be treated in keeping with the Geneva Conventions as well as Exhibit P23, i.e., the decision on the appointment of the civilian commissioner for the municipality of Srebrenica dated 11 July 1995. In this decision, in its paragraph 4, it is stated and I quote: "The commissioner will make sure that the civilian and military bodies, when it comes to all the citizens who participated in fighting the VRS, should be treated as prisoners of war. At the same time they will make sure that the civilian population can freely choose the place where they want to move to." Who is it who planned the evacuation of the population of Srebrenica? This can be seen in Exhibit D174, a document which was issued on the 11th of July, 1995. This is a telegram which Annan sent to Akashi and presents the UN policy towards the Srebrenica enclave. It consists of a complete evacuation of Srebrenica. In paragraph 2(B) of this document it is stated, inter alia, I quote: "UNHCR reports that 80 per cent to 90 per cent of the population of Srebrenica (the total number of the population is about 40.000 people) are made up of the displaced persons who had fled war activities at the beginning of the war so that they don't have any property in Srebrenica and they will not be attached to the enclave and they will be interested in leaving for Tuzla. One of the local UNHCR members in Srebrenica stated today that practically all the people there wanted to leave the enclaves." Somewhat later it is stated and I quote: "After the consultations with the Bosnian government in order to avoid the continuation of the humanitarian disaster, the Bosnian Serbs will be requested to allow all the population, including all the men, to leave Srebrenica and to go to Tuzla if they so wish. The Dutch Battalion will be instructed to remain in Srebrenica until the moment the departure of those people is agreed with the Bosnian Serbs." Under ideal circumstances, a considerable number of armed UNPROFOR members will stay in UNPROFOR at least until the moment everybody who wants to leave the enclave is gone. This operation will have to be co-ordinated with the desire of the Dutch Battalion to evacuate its own forces from Srebrenica as soon as possible. In paragraph 3 of this document it is said: "UNPROFOR," and I quote, "UNPROFOR shall immediately commence negotiations with the Bosnian Serbs about: "1.
